standard: DCAS v1.0 + SSDE Template README v1.1

checks.requirement: README.pdf must exist in the uppermost directory, in PDF format.
checks.detail: No README.pdf in the uppermost directory.

checks.requirement: README should follow the SSDE template (data availability & provenance, data sources, computational requirements, program-to-output map, instructions to replicators).
checks.detail: Missing sections: data availability, computational requirement, instructions, data source.

checks.requirement: A master script that runs the full package is strongly encouraged.
Software names+versions, packages+versions, and expected runtime must be stated (README or setup program).
checks.detail: README present to carry environment statement.

checks.requirement: Code must run with no manual intervention beyond a single directory-path edit (no scattered absolute paths).
Raw-to-analysis code must ship and run; analysis variables re-derived from raw, not from opaque derived files.
checks.detail: Static check cannot confirm raw-to-analysis re-derivation; author must confirm.

checks.requirement: More than 1000 files must be zipped; otherwise deposit unzipped.
Data and Code Availability Form (+ Information Form, Archive Agreement) required.
checks.detail: Complete the AEA Data and Code Availability Form (plus the Information Form and Archive Agreement) and submit them with the deposit.
checks.author_action: Complete the AEA Data and Code Availability Form (plus the Information Form and Archive Agreement) and submit them with the deposit.
checks.how: Fill the official forms; copy the data-availability and software statements from your README so they match.
checks.self_check: All three forms are submitted and their statements agree with the README.

checks.requirement: If data cannot be public: dual-package model + a synthetic/fake dataset for a functionality test.
checks.detail: If any data cannot be made public, build a dual package and add a synthetic/fake dataset that lets a reviewer run a functionality test.
checks.author_action: If any data cannot be made public, build a dual package and add a synthetic/fake dataset that lets a reviewer run a functionality test.
checks.how: Split into a public package (code + synthetic data) and a restricted package; document how the synthetic data mirrors the real schema.
checks.self_check: The package runs end to end on the synthetic data and produces the expected output shapes.
